pageContent: Andaman Islands ranks among Andaman and Nicobar Islands's most rewarding destinations, and it is easy to see why travelers keep returning. Known for emerald islands where the bay of bengal meets paradise, it packs a remarkable variety of experiences into one trip. When people search for the best places to visit in Andaman Islands, the headline names come up again and again: Radhanagar Beach, Cellular Jail National Memorial, Elephant Beach, Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep), Scuba Diving at Havelock Island. Each earns its spot for a reason — together they capture the beach, island, adventure character that defines the region.

Beyond the icons, the must visit places in Andaman Islands reward anyone willing to explore a little further. Spots such as Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island), Baratang Island Limestone Caves, North Bay Island, Kalapathar Beach, Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park, Wandoor round out an itinerary and show a different side of the destination. For the best experience, time your visit thoughtfully: many of the top tourist attractions in Andaman Islands are at their finest early in the day or around golden hour, when the light is soft, crowds are thin, and photographs come alive. Most travelers find that two to four unhurried days are enough to cover the essentials without rushing.

Looking for things to do in Andaman Islands that go beyond the guidebook? Seek out the quieter finds — Long Island, Ramnagar Beach, Diglipur, Wandoor Beach and Mangrove Boardwalk — where you will trade ticket queues for genuine local atmosphere. This curated guide is built to be the most useful starting point on the internet for your trip: every attraction below includes why it is worth your time, the best time to visit, a realistic duration, and a direct Google Maps search. Use it to shortlist your favourites, then drop them straight into a Trypinn itinerary, invite your crew, and turn a list of must-see places in Andaman Islands into a trip that actually happens.

Planning practicalities matter as much as the sights. A typical visit to Andaman Islands in Andaman and Nicobar Islands works best as a two-to-four-day trip, leaving room to slow down rather than tick boxes. Group the Radhanagar Beach and Cellular Jail National Memorial area together to cut travel time, and keep a relaxed half-day spare for the hidden gems and spontaneous detours that make beach and island and adventure so memorable. Whatever season you choose, book stays and any permits or tickets ahead during peak months, start early to beat the crowds, and carry the Google Maps links below so navigating between the best places to visit in Andaman Islands stays effortless from the first attraction to the last.

attractions.name: Radhanagar Beach
attractions.description: Consistently ranked among Asia's finest beaches, Radhanagar on Havelock Island stretches across 2 km of powdery white sand backed by dense evergreen forest. The water graduates from pale turquoise at the shore to deep indigo offshore. Sunsets here are legendary — the sky turns amber and crimson over the Andaman Sea, drawing crowds to the shoreline every evening.
attractions.whyVisit: Voted Asia's Best Beach by Time magazine, it offers a near-flawless combination of scenery, clean water, and atmosphere.
attractions.bestTime: October to May; sunsets are spectacular year-round

attractions.name: Cellular Jail National Memorial
attractions.description: Built by the British between 1896 and 1906, this seven-winged solitary confinement prison once housed India's most prominent freedom fighters, earning the grim nickname 'Kala Pani'. Three of the original wings still stand in Port Blair. The daily light-and-sound show narrates the harrowing stories of prisoners like Veer Savarkar with dramatic effect against the illuminated corridors.
attractions.whyVisit: A deeply moving memorial to India's independence struggle, essential for understanding the colonial era's brutality.
attractions.bestTime: Morning visits are less crowded; evening for the sound-and-light show

attractions.name: Elephant Beach
attractions.description: Accessible only by a 45-minute boat ride or a forest trek through Havelock Island, Elephant Beach rewards visitors with some of the Andamans' best shallow-water coral reefs. The water is so clear that snorkellers can spot turtles, parrotfish, and anemonefish without diving below the surface. The beach itself is narrow but pristine, shaded by overhanging trees.
attractions.whyVisit: The most accessible spot in the Andamans for world-class snorkelling without a diving certification.
attractions.bestTime: October to April, mornings for calmer water

attractions.name: Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep)
attractions.description: Smaller and quieter than Havelock, Neil Island is shaped by paddy fields, flower farms, and secluded coves. Its three main beaches — Bharatpur, Laxmanpur, and Sitapur — each have a distinct character, from the boat-jetty bustle of Bharatpur to the dramatic natural rock arch at Laxmanpur II visible only at low tide. Cycling between villages is the preferred pace of travel here.
attractions.whyVisit: The Andamans' most laid-back island, perfect for travellers seeking solitude over spectacle.
attractions.bestTime: November to February

attractions.name: Scuba Diving at Havelock Island
attractions.description: Havelock's dive sites include Dixon's Pinnacle, Johnny's Gorge, and Minerva's Ledge — featuring walls draped in soft coral, schools of barracuda, reef sharks, and the occasional manta ray. Water visibility often exceeds 20 metres. Both certified divers and first-timers on beginner dives operated by PADI centres like Barefoot Scuba can explore reefs at depths of 6 to 30 metres.
attractions.whyVisit: One of India's top scuba destinations with diverse marine life and excellent year-round visibility.
attractions.bestTime: December to April for best visibility

attractions.name: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island)
attractions.description: Once the British administrative headquarters of the Andamans, this small island a short ferry ride from Port Blair is now a haunting ruin reclaimed by nature. Banyan tree roots have split through the walls of the old church, bakery, and chief commissioner's house. Spotted deer roam freely among the crumbling colonnades, creating an eerie but beautiful tableau of nature versus empire.
attractions.whyVisit: An atmospheric open-air ruin-scape that vividly illustrates the island's colonial past.
attractions.bestTime: October to March, morning light is ideal for photography

attractions.name: Baratang Island Limestone Caves
attractions.description: Reached through a convoy crossing the Jarawa Tribal Reserve, Baratang's limestone caves are a geological wonder. Stalactites and stalagmites form cathedral-like chambers dripping with moisture. The journey itself — a speedboat through dense mangrove creeks followed by a forest walk — is as memorable as the caves. Mud volcanoes nearby bubble quietly with grey sludge year-round.
attractions.whyVisit: A rare combination of tribal reserve passage, mangrove waterways, and dramatic cave formations in one journey.
attractions.bestTime: October to March

attractions.name: North Bay Island
attractions.description: Just a 15-minute ferry from Port Blair, North Bay is the Andamans' most accessible coral reef experience. The island has a glass-bottom boat service for non-swimmers, a sea-walk facility where visitors don a helmet and walk on the seabed, and designated snorkelling zones. The lighthouse on the island's crest offers panoramic views of Port Blair harbour and the surrounding sea.
attractions.whyVisit: Ideal for families wanting a reef experience close to Port Blair with multiple water activity options.
attractions.bestTime: October to April

attractions.name: Kalapathar Beach
attractions.description: Named for the dark rocks (kala pathar means 'black stone') jutting from its southern end, this 2-km beach on Havelock Island is far less visited than Radhanagar yet equally striking. The black basalt boulders contrast dramatically against the white sand and turquoise sea. There are no facilities here — just the beach, the rocks, and the sound of waves breaking through the forest.
attractions.whyVisit: A pristine, crowd-free beach offering Havelock's most photogenic rock-and-sand contrast.
attractions.bestTime: Early morning for golden light on the black rocks

attractions.name: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park, Wandoor
attractions.description: Spread across 15 uninhabited islands and 281 sq km of sea off the southwest coast of South Andaman, this marine park protects one of India's richest coral ecosystems. Snorkelling trips depart from Wandoor jetty to Jolly Buoy and Red Skin islands, where visibility through the water reveals parrotfish, angelfish, sea turtles, and spectacular table corals. Boat trips are regulated to protect the reef.
attractions.whyVisit: The Andamans' most protected and biodiverse marine habitat, with strictly managed visitor numbers.
attractions.bestTime: Jolly Buoy open November to May only

attractions.name: Chidiya Tapu (Bird Island)
attractions.description: At the southernmost tip of South Andaman, Chidiya Tapu earns its 'Bird Island' name with sightings of the Andaman woodpecker, Andaman serpent eagle, and emerald dove in its dense mangrove and forest fringe. The sunset from the rocky promontory here is considered the best on the main island. A nature trail winds through the forest to a small beach.
attractions.whyVisit: The best birdwatching site on South Andaman combined with Port Blair's finest sunset viewpoint.
attractions.bestTime: Early morning for birds, evening for sunset

attractions.name: Samudrika Naval Marine Museum
attractions.description: Run by the Indian Navy in Port Blair, Samudrika houses five galleries covering Andaman's ecology, tribal culture, marine life, and the islands' geological history. A real whale skeleton is suspended from the ceiling of the natural history wing. Aquarium tanks display the islands' live marine species, and detailed dioramas of Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa, and Sentinelese tribes provide rare anthropological insight.
attractions.whyVisit: The most comprehensive overview of Andaman's natural and cultural heritage in a single visit.
attractions.bestTime: Any time; mornings are quieter

attractions.name: Diglipur and Saddle Peak
attractions.description: In North Andaman, Diglipur is the base for trekking to Saddle Peak — at 732 metres the highest point in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The five-hour return trail through tropical rainforest passes through the Saddle Peak National Park, home to saltwater crocodiles, Andaman wild pigs, and numerous endemic birds. Nearby Ramnagar Beach is a nesting site for leatherback sea turtles.
attractions.whyVisit: The islands' most challenging trek combined with rare wildlife encounters and turtle-nesting beaches.
attractions.bestTime: December to February

attractions.name: Havelock Island to Neil Island Ferry Route
attractions.description: The government and private ferry routes between Havelock and Neil islands pass through open sea channels flanked by forested islands with no development visible in any direction. Flying fish leap alongside the bow, and spinner dolphins frequently ride the bow wave. On clear days, the water below the ferry is translucent enough to see the sea floor in the shallower passages.
attractions.whyVisit: One of the most scenic short ferry crossings in India, with near-guaranteed dolphin sightings.
attractions.bestTime: Morning departures for calmer seas

attractions.name: Anthropological Museum Port Blair
attractions.description: This small but significant museum on M.G. Road in Port Blair is dedicated to the indigenous tribal communities of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands — the Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa, Sentinelese, Nicobarese, and Shompen. Exhibits include tools, canoes, ornaments, and photographs documenting pre-contact life. It remains one of the few places where outsiders can legally learn about the Sentinelese people.
attractions.whyVisit: Irreplaceable resource for understanding the islands' ancient and isolated tribal cultures.
attractions.bestTime: Weekday mornings

attractions.name: Corbyn's Cove Beach
attractions.description: The closest beach to Port Blair city, Corbyn's Cove is a crescent of soft sand fringed by coconut palms just 7 km from the airport. While not as spectacular as Havelock's beaches, it is well maintained with showers, cafes, and water sport concessions offering jet skiing and banana boat rides. It is the most practical option for an early-morning swim or evening stroll during a Port Blair stopover.
attractions.whyVisit: Port Blair's most convenient beach for a quick swim or sundowner without taking a ferry.
attractions.bestTime: Evening for cool breeze and sunset views

attractions.name: Bharatpur Beach, Neil Island
attractions.description: Located adjacent to the Neil Island jetty, Bharatpur is the island's most sheltered beach, protected by a coral reef that keeps the water exceptionally calm — ideal for young children. Colourful coral heads are visible through the water without even snorkelling. Local boat operators offer glass-bottom rides, and the beach has basic shacks serving fresh seafood.
attractions.whyVisit: The calmest and safest swimming beach in the Andamans, perfect for families with children.
attractions.bestTime: October to April

attractions.name: Limestone Natural Arch, Laxmanpur Beach
attractions.description: At the western end of Neil Island's Laxmanpur II Beach, the sea has carved a graceful natural arch through a limestone headland. It is only fully visible during low tide, when the rock platform around it is exposed and walkable. The arch frames the open sea perfectly, making it one of the Andamans' most photographed natural landmarks. Sunset light turns the limestone gold and orange.
attractions.whyVisit: A rare sea-carved natural arch that creates the islands' most dramatic sunset photography composition.
attractions.bestTime: Low tide at sunset — check tide tables in advance

attractions.name: Jolly Buoy Island
attractions.description: Part of the Marine National Park, Jolly Buoy is an uninhabited island open only from November to May to allow reef recovery during monsoon. It has no permanent infrastructure — visitors arrive by boat, snorkel the pristine reef in designated zones, and leave by afternoon. Plastic and food are banned on the island. The coral cover here is among the densest and most intact in the entire Andamans.
attractions.whyVisit: The most strictly protected snorkelling site in the Andamans with the highest density of intact coral.
attractions.bestTime: November to May only; open on alternate days with Red Skin Island

attractions.name: Vijaynagar Beach (Beach No. 5), Havelock
attractions.description: Often simply called Beach No. 5, Vijaynagar on the eastern side of Havelock Island is a long, gently curving shore where most of the island's upscale resorts are located. The beach is calmer than Radhanagar, faces east for brilliant sunrises, and has excellent swimming conditions. The sea here teems with bioluminescent plankton on dark nights from June to September.
attractions.whyVisit: The best beach on Havelock for sunrise and the only reliable spot for bioluminescent sea at night.
attractions.bestTime: Sunrise; or monsoon nights for bioluminescence

attractions.name: Mud Volcano, Baratang
attractions.description: Among only a handful of onshore mud volcanoes in all of South and Southeast Asia, the Baratang mud volcanoes are low mounds of grey clay that bubble intermittently as geothermal gases escape through the sediment. They are not dramatic in scale but are geologically fascinating — the largest bubbles rise 15-20 cm above the surface. They sit in a forest clearing a short walk from the limestone caves.
attractions.whyVisit: One of India's rarest geological phenomena, easily combined with the Baratang limestone cave trip.
attractions.bestTime: October to March (accessed through Jarawa Reserve convoy)

attractions.name: Aberdeen Bazaar, Port Blair
attractions.description: The commercial heart of Port Blair, Aberdeen Bazaar is a dense grid of shops selling Andaman pearls, black coral jewellery (from licensed traders), handmade shell crafts, coconut wood products, and the famous Andaman padauk timber objects. Street food stalls serve fish tikka and local coconut-based snacks in the evening. The bazaar is also the best place to arrange ferry tickets and island tours.
attractions.whyVisit: The only place in the islands to buy authentic Andaman pearls and local craft souvenirs at competitive prices.
attractions.bestTime: Evening, when the food stalls set up

attractions.name: Long Island
attractions.description: Largely bypassed by tourist itineraries, Long Island requires a ferry from Rangat on Middle Andaman and rewards persistence with two exceptional beaches: Lalaji Bay — accessible only by a 45-minute forest trek — and the easily reached Guitar Island sandbar. The island has basic guesthouses, almost no commercial tourism, and mangrove-lined creeks ideal for kayaking at dawn.
attractions.whyVisit: The most unspoiled large island accessible to independent travellers in the entire Andaman chain.
attractions.bestTime: November to March

attractions.name: Ramnagar Beach, Diglipur
attractions.description: This remote beach in North Andaman is one of India's most important nesting sites for the giant leatherback sea turtle — the world's largest reptile, reaching up to 2 metres in length. Between January and March, nesting females haul themselves ashore at night to lay eggs. The Forest Department runs strictly supervised night-watch camps. The beach itself is wild and undeveloped, backed by rainforest.
attractions.whyVisit: One of India's only legally accessible leatherback turtle nesting beaches, a once-in-a-lifetime wildlife encounter.
attractions.bestTime: January to March for turtle nesting

attractions.name: Wandoor Beach and Mangrove Boardwalk
attractions.description: Wandoor village on South Andaman's west coast is the departure point for Marine National Park boat trips, but the beach and adjacent mangrove boardwalk are worth visiting independently. The elevated walkway winds through a dense stand of Rhizophora mangroves where mudskippers, fiddler crabs, and kingfishers are reliably seen. The beach itself is a quiet, clean alternative to Port Blair's crowded Corbyn's Cove.
attractions.whyVisit: A tranquil combination of mangrove ecology walk and uncrowded beach just 29 km from Port Blair.
attractions.bestTime: Morning for wildlife on the boardwalk
